units.title: Cutoffs preserve mass, entropy and gradient energy in the limit
units.classification: Canonical extraction of an existing generic proof; not new Gaussian mathematics
units.statement: Let E be any complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure, and let mu be any measure. Suppose f:E→R is genuinely C2, f and its true gradient belong to L2(mu), and f² log(f²) is integrable. Let chi_R be the existing radial smooth cutoff at radius R, and set f_n=chi_(n+1)*f. Then the integrals of f_n², f_n² log(f_n²), and ||gradient f_n||² converge respectively to those of f², f² log(f²), and ||gradient f||². Finite dimension, probability, finite total measure, positivity and nonzero function mass are not required.
units.formula: f_n=\chi_{n+1}f,\qquad \left(\int f_n^2,\ \int\Phi(f_n^2),\ \int\|\nabla f_n\|^2\right)\longrightarrow\left(\int f^2,\ \int\Phi(f^2),\ \int\|\nabla f\|^2\right),\quad\Phi(q)=q\log q,\ \Phi(0)=0.
assumptions: The measure is arbitrary. The three actual analytic domains, not finiteness of mu(E), provide the integrable envelopes. All integrals in the formula are with respect to the same mu.

The gradient is Mathlib's actual Hilbert gradient of the given C2 representative. Its L2 premise includes a.e. strong measurability. A totalized derivative value alone would not establish genuine differentiability.

The cutoff equals1 on the ball of radius R, lies in [0,1], vanishes outside radius2R and has derivative norm at most K/R for one fixed cutoff constant K. In infinite dimension this does not assert compact support; finite dimension enters the later compact-test application, not these limits.

steps.title: Make all approximants measurable
steps.text: The radial cutoff is smooth. Multiplying it by the C2 function gives a C2 approximant, so its square and square-log-square are measurable. The squared norm of its genuine gradient is continuous and real-valued. The assumptions on f and its gradient give the two square integrability inputs.
steps.lean: hfn constructs ContDiff; hf2.integrable_sq and memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq_norm give im and ie. Continuity supplies a.e. strong measurability of the real integrands.

steps.title: Pass the square mass through the integral
steps.text: The cutoff values tend to1, while their absolute values never exceed1. Thus f_n² converges pointwise to f² and is dominated by the already integrable f². Dominated convergence, not pointwise convergence alone, proves the first integral limit.
steps.lean: radialSmoothCutoff_tendsto_one supplies hft. The first tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence invocation uses im as its actual dominator.

steps.title: Control entropy even where the function vanishes
steps.text: Put a=chi_(n+1)² and q=f². The product identity for q log q gives a uniform dilation bound including a=0 and q=0. Its right side is integrable by the entropy and mass hypotheses. Continuity of Phi at zero gives pointwise convergence without assuming that f is nonzero.
steps.lean: The private entropy_dilation_bound proves this scalar estimate from Real.negMulLog_mul. The second DCT uses hp.abs.add im and Real.continuous_mul_log, not continuity of log at zero.

steps.title: Use genuine derivatives and one energy envelope
steps.text: Differentiate the actual product. The cutoff and derivative bounds, with n+1≥1, give one integrable envelope independent of n. No second derivative estimate or integration-by-parts theorem is used.
steps.lean: gradient_mul uses the differentiability premises of fderiv_fun_mul. cutoff_energy_bound transports the derivative norm through the Hilbert Riesz isometry and proves the displayed quadratic estimate.

steps.title: Use local plateaus, then the third dominated limit
steps.text: At each fixed point x, sufficiently large cutoffs equal1 on a neighborhood of x. The gradients of f_n and f are then exactly equal at x. This local fact justifies gradient convergence; convergence of cutoff values by itself would not. The energy envelope from the previous step completes the final DCT.
steps.lean: cutoff_gradient_eventually_eq proves neighborhood equality and applies EventuallyEq.gradient_eq. The final DCT combines this with the integrable energy envelope.

units.title: Extend compact smooth LSI to its actual analytic domain
units.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel structure, mu any measure, and C a fixed real number. Suppose Ent_mu(v²)≤2C integral||gradient v||² for every compactly supported infinitely smooth real v. Then the same inequality holds for every infinitely smooth f with f and gradient f in L2(mu) and f² log(f²) integrable. Here Ent_mu(q) is literally integral(q log q) minus (integral q) log(integral q), with0 log0=0; it is not a silently normalized entropy for a general measure.
units.formula:
\left[ orall v\in C_c^\infty(E),\ \operatorname{Ent}_\mu(v^2)\le2C\int\|
abla v\|^2\,d\muight]\Longrightarrow\operatorname{Ent}_\mu(f^2)\le2C\int\|
abla f\|^2\,d\mu,\quad f\in C^\infty\cap L^2,\ 
abla f\in L^2,\ \Phi(f^2)\in L^1.
assumptions: The assumed test class is exactly compact C-infinity, not compact C2. Requiring LSI on the larger C2 test class would strengthen the source premise.
Finite dimension is used to make the radial approximants compactly supported. Their smoothness is genuine, not inferred from a totalized derivative.

C is fixed independently of the approximating index. A sign restriction on C or positive function mass is not needed merely to pass these real limits. Probability normalization, canonical scores and semigroups are absent.

The three analytic-domain hypotheses are inputs of this canonical extension lemma. The eventual source Exercise1.7 Anchor must derive them for its actual square-root test; they are not extra exercise premises.

steps.title: Build admissible compact smooth tests
steps.text: Take f_n=chi_(n+1)*f. The cutoff is infinitely smooth and compactly supported in finite dimension, so the product is an actual member of the assumed test class. There is no assertion that f itself is compactly supported.
steps.lean: radialSmoothCutoff_contDiff.mul hf preserves the source smooth order. radialSmoothCutoff_hasCompactSupport.mul_right proves compact support of the product.

steps.title: Apply only the given compact inequality
steps.text: The source premise applies to each actual f_n. This does not assume the desired inequality for the noncompact function. The existing generic cutoff theorem can use f's weaker C2 consequence without changing the C-infinity class to which LSI is applied.
steps.lean: hcompact (fn n) consumes the newly constructed smoothness and support proofs. hfC2 is used only for cutoff_integral_limits.

steps.title: Reuse all three actual integral limits
steps.text: Apply the shared cutoff theorem with the given L2, gradient-L2 and entropy-integrability inputs. It proves convergence of mass, entropy integrand and energy internally, with the measurable integrands and integrable envelopes explained above.
steps.formula: m_n\to m,\qquad p_n\to p,\qquad e_n\to e,\quad m_n=\int f_n^2,\ p_n=\int\Phi(f_n^2),\ e_n=\int\|\nabla f_n\|^2.
steps.lean: cutoff_integral_limits returns hm, hp and he. No convergence hypothesis or asserted domain certificate is introduced.

steps.title: Keep the normalization term valid at zero
steps.text: Although log alone is not continuous at zero, Phi(q)=q log q is. Consequently Phi(m_n) converges to Phi(m), including m=0. Subtract this from the entropy-integrand limit; no division by mass or positivity branch is necessary.
steps.lean: Real.continuous_mul_log transports hm, and hp.sub forms the actual entropy limit. This is not a separate invalid log(m_n) limit.

steps.title: Pass the inequality through closed real order
steps.text: The coefficient2C is fixed, so2C e_n tends to2C e for any real C. Passing the already valid compact inequalities to these two limits yields the asserted inequality on f, with the same constant.
steps.lean: he.const_mul (2*C) and le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto close the inequality. There is no constant deterioration or appeal to unproved domain closure.

steps.title: See the actual square-root consumer, without claiming PI
steps.text: In the focused finite-measure example, the existing bounded smooth compact-gradient producer constructs u_epsilon=sqrt(1+epsilon*f), its smoothness, L2, entropy and Frechet energy. Riesz norm equality and genuine gradient measurability turn that energy into gradient-L2 internally. The new theorem then supplies LSI for u_epsilon. Centering the source test, identifying normalized entropy, taking the quadratic limits and proving PI/core closure remain separate work.
